subject: Request: deterministic throughput window for dedicated pool - VerdantHealth
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@verdanthealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: deterministic throughput window for dedicated pool - VerdantHealth

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this — we’ve been working with Redwood Dedicated for the last six months and overall it’s been great. Over the last two sprints we’ve started seeing repeated tail latency during our EOD inference batch (approx 18:00–18:30 PT) that correlates with a third-party reporting spike in customer churn scoring. When latency spikes into the 2–3s per request range, our application falls out of SLA and downstream consumers retry aggressively, which multiplies the load and has caused a partial outage for a 45-minute window last Wednesday.

We understand Dedicated isn’t intended to be a hard real-time system, but for this specific 30-minute nightly window we need deterministic throughput to keep latency under 600ms P95. Can Redwood provide an operational variance or short-term amendment that: 
- Guarantees a minimum concurrent-token throughput for a named dedicated pool for a 30-minute nightly window (we can agree on a 6–8 node equivalent),
- Clarifies preemption behavior (we need zero preemptions during that window), and
- Defines credits/credits-back if the window fails to meet the promised throughput/latency.

We can share the traffic sample and a short summary of the downstream impact (attached). We’re hoping to avoid wholesale migration of that pipeline, and instead request a targeted SLA amendment or carve-out for the nightly window.

Can we schedule a 45-minute call this week to scope a pragmatic approach (pilot + runbook + commercial terms)?

Best,
Sara
Sara Lopez
Director, Platform Engineering — VerdantHealth

Attachment: verdant_traffic_q1-q2.csv (anonymized sample of request latencies and counts)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@verdanthealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deterministic throughput window for dedicated pool - VerdantHealth

Sara — thanks for the clear write-up and for sending the sample. Im sorry to hear you hit that outage window; we take these incidents seriously. I talked this over with product and operations and here are practical options we can propose quickly: 

1) Nightly deterministic reservation (preferred): Reserve a fixed set of reserved-GPU capacity for VerdantHealth for 30 minutes each night. We can set a soft-preemption rule (0 preemptions during the window) and pin those nodes to your pool. This requires a short contract addendum and a small committed uplift.

2) Priority tokens + burst buffer: Configure priority tokens for the named pool and a dedicated burst buffer that auto-allocates when your queueing depth crosses the threshold. This is lower-friction operationally and can be implemented faster, but is not a hard guarantee.

3) Hybrid pilot: 2-week pilot where we run (2) with aggressive observability + a dry-run of (1) for one night to validate scheduling and cost. If pilot metrics show continued exposure, we transition to (1).

Commercials: for (1) wed propose a 3-month trial addendum with a service credit ladder tied to P95 latency and a capped credit pool. For (2) the uplift is usage-based with a small nightly minimum.

Next steps I propose: 1) scoping call (45m) to confirm the window, node sizing, and instrumentation; 2) well produce a one-page Mutual Action Plan and a pilot runbook (I attached a first draft); 3) legal drafts a short amendment for the reservation.

Are you available Tue 06/08 11:00–11:45 PT or Wed 06/09 09:00–09:45 PT? Irene (CS lead) and Ben (Sales) are on copy to help with instrumentation and commercial terms.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_map_verdant_v1.docx; pilot_runbook_v0.2.pdf

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: VerdantHealth nightly deterministic window — legal touchpoint

Forwarding Verdants ask — they want a nightly 30-minute reservation with zero preemptions. Ops confirms feasibility but well need a short SLA addendum (term, sizing, credits ladder). Ben: can you coordinate commercial suggestion? Legal: please prepare a 1-page amendment template we can use as a starting point (term, failure credits, measurement method: P95 latency measured from Redwood tracing with Verdant token tags).

Quick context: Verdant is in production, mid-market healthcare; impact is a churn-score pipeline that multiplies customer rescoring requests if it stalls. Theyre asking for guaranteed throughput during a small window rather than continuous reservation.

Im proposing to run the hybrid pilot next week; will confirm after they pick a call slot.

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@verdanthealth.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: platform@verdanthealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deterministic throughput window for dedicated pool - VerdantHealth

Mateo — thanks for the quick options. Tue 06/08 11:00 PT works for us (joining: myself, Priya Patel, and our SRE lead).

Two quick asks ahead of the call: 
- Can you surface what observability events you will use to measure P95 for the amendment (traces, token-level counters, or ingestion counts)? Wed like the measurement to be traceable to our request tokens.
- Regarding credits: if we opt for (1) and the window fails twice in a month, we will expect a proportional credit and a remediation plan (not just reporting). Can you confirm Redwood is open to a remediations clause?

Attached is the traffic dump and a short post-incident note; the file shows the retry storms that started at ~18:03 PT last Wednesday. Also, please include a quick sketch of the node sizing youd recommend for a 600ms P95 objective so our infra team can validate.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Sara Lopez
Director, Platform Engineering
VerdantHealth

Attachment: verdant_traffic_q1-q2.csv

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@verdanthealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deterministic throughput window for dedicated pool - VerdantHealth

Great, thanks — call is set. Quick summary and commitments before the meeting so were aligned: 

1) Measurement: We will use token-tagged tracing (Redwood request_id + Verdant customer_token) + per-node request counters. SLA measurement will be P95 latency across the tagged requests during the 30-minute window, as measured by Redwoods tracing backend. We will provide the exact query and a sampling dashboard before the pilot starts.

2) Remediation & credits: Redwood is open to a remediation clause for reservations. Proposed draft: a graduated credit schedule (first failure: written remediation + 10% usage credit for the nightly window; second failure within 30 days: 25% credit + optional escalation review). Legal will provide wording.

3) Pilot + sizing: Ops recommends starting pilot with a 4-GPU equivalent reservation (weve modelled your traffic from the sample file). During the pilot well run an experimental dry-run of the 0-preemption policy for one night to validate scheduler behavior. If the dry-run shows an obvious resource shortfall well scale to 6-GPU equivalent.

4) Action items: 
- Redwood (Mateo): send MAP + pilot runbook update and a sizing sketch (by EOD Tue).
- Verdant (Sara): confirm SRE attendees and any additional telemetry tags (by Tue morning).
- Legal/Finance (Ben & legal): prepare 1-page SLA addendum draft for review (Ben can share a preliminary commercial).

Ill upload the MAP + runbook and open a DocuSign room for the amendment after our call. Link will be shared in this thread.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Mateo
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
